messages.subject: Labeling error with scale_y_datetime()
parts:
I'm new to ggplot2 and R, so apologies if this is already dealt with
somewhere.

I'm trying to produce a scatterplot of web traffic data from a date-
time series, plotting dates on the x axis and times of day on the y
axis. (I'm following a suggestion at
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/7160565/how-to-create-a-time-scatterplot-with-r.)
The y-axis is formatted with scale_y_datetime().

The y axis formatting works well, but a 12:00 AM time-of-day causes
the y axis labels to be shifted so that the origin of the y axis is
marked "18:00".

Here's a sample data set:

2011 Oct 02, 12:00 AM
2011 Oct 03, 06:00 AM
2011 Oct 04, 11:30 AM

And here are the relevant bits of code, somewhat simplified:

dt <- as.POSIXct(strptime(data, format='%Y %b %d, %I:%M %p'))
date <- trunc (dt, 'day')
time <- difftime(dt, date)
df <- data.frame(date, time)
p <- ggplot(df, aes(x=date, y=time))
p + geom_point() + scale_y_datetime()

Changing line 1 of the data to "12:01 AM" causes scale_y_datetime() to
behave correctly.

Is this a bug, or is there a setting that I need to take account of?

Many thanks for any help, etc.,

Fraser

ggplot doesn't handle times directly; it can handle dates and datetimes,
but not just times. The answer in the question you linked to to use
scale_y_datetime is not a good one. Rather, you need to build the axis
and labels yourself.

data <- c(
"2011 Oct 02, 12:00 AM",
"2011 Oct 03, 06:00 AM",
"2011 Oct 04, 11:30 AM")

df <- data.frame(date=as.Date(date), time=as.numeric(time))
ggplot(df, aes(x=date, y=time)) +
geom_point() +
scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,86400),
breaks=seq(0,86400,by=10800),
labels=paste(seq(0,24,by=3),":00",sep=""))

Things I did differently:
* converted date to a pure Date, rather than a datetime with a time of
midnight
* treat time as a raw number of seconds
* manually format the y axis specifying breaks (every 3 hours = 10800
seconds) and labels ("0:00", "3:00", etc).

Senior Research Associate, Department of Surgery
Oregon Health & Science University

Thank you! I found that my R kit did the as.numeric(time) conversion
inconsistently as far as units, so it worked better (and more
readably) in the end to do:

> time <- difftime(datetimes, date, units="hours")
> …
> …scale_y_continuous(name="Time of day", limits=c(0,24), breaks=seq(0,24,by=3), labels=paste(seq(0,24,by=3),":00",sep=""))…
